features.description:
The device manager now includes a new cookbook section.
The cookbook includes a number of example usecases derived from our new end-to-end testing framework,
with interactive demos and detailed information about the setup used.

You can now use a single key as an input to a chord.
This feature must be enabled in the settings first via the minimum chord key count setting.

You can now add chords with ARPEGGIATE + key -> ... to create custom arpeggiates.
The previously hard-coded arpeggiates can be added back by adding the "arpeggiates"
default chords in the device manager's library tab.

Overriding modifiers with exact chords is now also possible
when using the modifier as an arpeggiate after the chord.
Control what the concatenator between chords is using the new <kbd>HYPERSPACE</kbd> and <kbd>CAPTURE</kbd> actions.

You can now select "prepended" as a concatenation style.
This mode is part of the Hyperspace feature, and recommended for text editing (like coding).
Instead of placing the space after chords (default), it is prepended to the subsequent chord.
This means you don't have to erase extra spaces while editing.

Adds universal VIM motion emulation through the <kbd>VIM</kbd> action.
This mode makes use of standard shortcuts like <kbd>CTRL</kbd><kbd>RIGHT</kbd>
(or <kbd>⌘</kbd> on Mac) to emulate VIM motions in a best-effort way in any
textbox. While not as powerful as native VIM or even just a VIM plugin,
you don't always have the option to use either of them,
so this is a way to carry around your VIM muscle memory to nearly every textbox you encounter.

Modifiers (like Shift or layer keys) normally only work if you press them before the key you want to modify, and release them before pressing any key you don’t want modified.
Fuzzy modifiers relax this rule: they let you press or release the modifier at almost the same time as the key. Instead of requiring a strict order, the system just checks whether the modifier’s press or release happened close enough in time to the key press.

In the past we've had both ASCII and KSC_... actions, which caused a lot of confusion to which
ones you are supposed to use and if there's any difference.
Adding to that confusion, CCX as the only device also used these actions by default in its chord library
and layout, making transferring and sharing libraries between X and Lite practically impossible.
We've made the decision to finally remove all KSC_... actions which are duplicates of ASCII actions.
Layouts are automatically migrated with no action required, for technical reasons however it is not
possible to migrate chord libraries in the same way. Use `CML CE` to auto-fix the library.
For gaming profiles we added a "layer warp" setting which re-presses held keys when you switch layers.
Grammar rules have been updated with community contributions. You can submit your own on our Issue Repo.

features.summary: DUP can now be used with modifiers
features.description: When typing "a" hitting shift + DUP now produces "A"
Enabling this might improve stability on certain hardware combinations.
Reducing this to 6-key might improve compatibility with older hardware.

Added a new Serial API command `CML CE` that auto-fixes issues in the chord library, such as
duplicate chords, usage of old/removed action codes, bad chord inputs, duplicate chord inputs and suspicious corrupted chords
(ÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿÿ chords).
Please make a backup before using this command.
LEDs now smoothly fade on and off.

features.summary: DUP now re-presses keys instead of continuing to hold them

features.description:
Auto-space rules have been simplified.
Auto-spaces are always applied unless <kbd>KSC_00</kbd> is present at the end of the chord.
Chords old chords are auto-upgraded.
Pre-3.0.0 backups need to be upgraded manually!

Settings/layout storage has been moved from onboard flash to the external flash
(same where the chords live).
When first updating this will cause a factory reset,
however following this update settings and layout will no longer be wiped when updating.

features.summary: Arpeggiated chord modifiers can be disabled separately

features.description:
Support for three Profiles has been added, each with their own layout and settings.
You can combine this feature with dynamic libraries as well by creating a
profile activation chord that simultaneously activates your desired dynamic library.

fixes.summary: Incorrect max chord count
fixes.description:
In a past update it was incorrectly stated that the maximum chord count was increased to 16k.
The actual increase was to 10,240.
We already put a great deal of care towards optimization,
but due to the very limited amount of RAM,
further reductions in maximum chord count can happen in the future as a tradeoff for new features.

fixes.summary: Memory corruption when approaching chord limit
fixes.description:
This issue could cause memory corruption when approaching the limit of 10,240 chords,
approximately starting around 9000 chords.

fixes.summary: Improved flash performance
Capitalize action is not interrupted by chentry
NULL is now ignored as an action
fixes.description:
Subsequently modifiers that use layer keys now no longer break backspacing when the target layer has no actions
on part of the chord input keys.

fixes.summary: Stuck key mitigation
fixes.description:
As a general fallback measure against (software-)stuck keys we added a measure that releases
all keys when you either physically release all switches or at the end of a chord.

fixes.summary: Specific compounds caused library corruption
fixes.description: There was a bug that could cause library corruption if you got unlucky that has now been fixed. This only compound chords with a specific base. you can check if your library contained any of these here.

fixes.summary: Can't use modifiers with chords that change concatenators
Smart detection erases newlines
Removed RST STARTER/FUNC commands
fixes.description: Factory chords are now added via the device manager/firmware meta api instead.

fixes.summary: RST CLEARCML/FACTORY/OTA will now force release all held keys before proceeding
Mouse move/click actions are now breaking actions
Removed obsolete "character entry" option, use "enable chording" option instead.
Potential improved USB Hub compatibility
Fixed device names in the manager popup
Poll rate setting
fixes.description:
Replaced the mouse/keyboard poll rate settings (which didn't actually change the poll rate) with a USB poll rate setting
under a new experimental category

fixes.summary: Fixed swapped Right Shift and Quote keys
Disconnect issues
fixes.description:
We've identified a potential workaround for intermittent disconnects on primarily MacOS and Windows,
available as the "aggressive reporting" setting.
We're still continuing to investigate as we gather feedback from this change.

fixes.summary: Leds can now be fully turned off
Fixed swapped Right Shift and Quote keys

features.description: You can now start typing on your device immediately while the chords load in the background. The CCOS is ready. message has been removed.
If you are okay with a bit more latency while typing this mode allows you to chord without backspacing.
Auto delete is now smarter and can be properly set to just delete chord inputs.
A single action to delete the last chord, last attempt, or just act as backspace.
Quickfix that auto-deletes all attempts until you successfully chord.

You can now (almost) create custom arpeggiates through chords.
The old arpeggiates just use JOIN and CAPITALIZE actions and act as a chord internally.
By default DUP will now only repeat printable keys (i.e. not backspace or arrow keys) so that it can be safely used in chord inputs. The previous behaviour is still available as DUP_ALL.
This feature was contributed by @gex__ as part of our communal source program, thank you!

This feature allows you to dedicate a stick to scrolling,
and scroll by spinning it like a scroll wheel instead of holding down a key.
We now provide a set of actions that hold AltGr+... and can be assigned to your layout directly.
This feature expands upon a bug we had before. You can now assign a different layer key to the target layer to toggle a layer on or off.
For easier and faster development every CCOS build now contains a meta.json file, which includes action codes, settings, changelog, firmware, factory defaults and more.

fixes.summary: Shift key not being held through layers
Fixed keyboard poll rate setting
